evidence.detail: Exact v308 rs/g/b is the abstract client timing base with exactly reset/mark semantics plus an int-returning wait(cycleMillis,minSleepMillis) style operation used by the AWT game loop.
rs/C stores this base as the active game-loop clock and its factory returns rs/g/d first with rs/g/c as fallback.
RuneScape/OpenOSRS deobfuscations preserve this exact hierarchy as Clock with concrete MilliClock and NanoClock implementations.

candidates.note: Recovered long-standing RuneScape client timing hierarchy identity.

evidence.detail: Exact v308 rs/g/c extends Clock and owns the classic ten-entry long timestamp history plus 256/1 rate-step fields used by the millisecond cycle scheduler.
The implementation is backed by a monotonicized System.currentTimeMillis() helper and recalculates sleep/rate from the ten-sample history before returning the number of client cycles to process.
The AWT game-loop factory constructs MilliClock when NanoClock construction fails.
Public RuneScape deobfuscations identify the same ten-long-array Clock subtype as MilliClock.

candidates.note: Recovered RuneScape MilliClock identity from exact structural and game-loop factory match.

evidence.detail: Exact v308 rs/g/d extends Clock, initializes its timing state from System.nanoTime() and advances cycle deadlines in nanoseconds.
The AWT game-loop factory prefers this implementation and invokes it through the Clock base on every client loop iteration.
Its wait operation computes nanosecond cycle duration from the requested millisecond period, sleeps when ahead and returns the number of due game cycles, capped at ten.
Public RuneScape deobfuscations identify the System.nanoTime-backed Clock subtype as NanoClock.

candidates.note: Recovered RuneScape NanoClock identity. SpawnPK contains local scheduling modifications but retains the same core class role.

evidence.detail: rs/g/e contains one public static long-millisecond sleep operation and no other runtime state or responsibility.
For positive delays divisible by 10, the helper sleeps delay-1 milliseconds and then 1 millisecond; otherwise it performs one Thread.sleep(delay), matching the timing clocks' shared sleep path.
Both rs/g/c and rs/g/d invoke this helper from their client-clock wait implementations; no unrelated exact-v308 consumer was found.

candidates.note: SleepUtil is descriptive exact-behavior recovery for the clock family's shared millisecond Thread.sleep wrapper. Confidence is 0.998.
